title: Checking of Refrigeration System with Manifold Gauge

content.text: This is a method in which the trouble is located by using a manifold gauge.
Read the manifold gauge pressure with the following established conditions:

items: (a) Temperature at the air inlet is 30 – 35°C (86 – 95°F)
(e) Temperature control lever set at cool

content.text: It should be noted that the gauge indications may vary slightly due to ambient temperature conditions.

content.description: Manifold gauge set showing two pressure gauges (LO for low pressure and HI for high pressure) connected to the AC system with three valve connections at the bottom

content.text: Low pressure side 1.5 – 2.0 kg/cm² (21 – 28 psi, 147 – 196 kPa)
High pressure side 14.5 – 15.0 kg/cm² (206 – 213 psi, 1,422 – 1,471 kPa)

content.description: Manifold gauge set showing two pressure gauges (LO for low pressure and HI for high pressure) connected to the AC system with three valve connections at the bottom, similar to first diagram

content.text: Condition: Periodically cools and then fails to cool

rows: During operation, pressure at low pressure side sometimes becomes a vacuum and sometimes normal
Moisture entered in refrigeration system freezes at expansion valve orifice and temporarily stops cycle, but normal state is restored after a time when the ice melts
Drier in oversaturated state ↓ Moisture in refrigeration system freezes at expansion valve orifice and blocks circulation of refrigerant

(1) Replace receiver and drier
(2) Remove moisture in cycle through repeated vacuum purging
(3) Charge new refrigerant to proper amount
